evals.prompt: Run a Varde scan on this repository and explain what to do with error, warning, and info findings.
evals.expected_output: Runs the scan, checks command, analysis, and gate status separately, then applies the contract: fix errors, fix warnings in code being touched or report them, and use info only as context. It does not start a code review or review gates.
assertions: Runs the scan and checks analysis and gate status separately from command success
States the distinct required action for error, warning, and info
Does not start a code review or review gates

evals.prompt: The scan says index_missing. What should happen next?
evals.expected_output: Restores code-index readiness according to whether the agent is a coordinator or worker. A worker does not build the index and reports scan capability unavailable if readiness cannot be restored.
assertions: Restores index readiness on the main checkout before rescanning
Does not have a worker build the index
Reports the limitation if the scan remains unavailable

evals.prompt: Save these scan decisions so the next scan can update them: F-17 is unsafe-query, error, src/db.rs:27, and was fixed; F-18 is generated-code, warning, src/generated/db.rs:8, and is not real because the code is a test fixture.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the working path with varde setup paths --json and writes one line per finding to <working>/scan/findings.md using id, rule, path and line, severity, and disposition. It updates by finding ID on repeat scans.
assertions: Uses the specified pipe-separated findings format
Persists the ledger under the working path from varde setup paths --json
Uses fixed and not-real dispositions with a concise reason for the latter
Updates existing IDs instead of duplicating findings

evals.prompt: A `varde scan` finding remains for the user after triage: `rule_id=unsafe-query`, `severity=warning`, `data.rules.unsafe-query.message=Unsanitized query input` (no finding-level message), `location.file=src/db.rs`, `location.span.start_line=27`, and `data.rules.unsafe-query.remediation=Use a parameterized query`. How is it retained, and what happens if the same scan is run again?
evals.expected_output: Applies the severity contract: because the warning remains outside code being touched, reports it and records one pipe-separated line in <working>/scan/findings.md using the scan-provided finding id, unsafe-query, src/db.rs:27, warning, and a concise left: reason. Uses the static rule message and remediation to explain the finding. A repeat scan updates the same finding ID instead of adding a duplicate; fixed and not-real findings are not persisted.
assertions: A leftover warning outside code being touched is reported and mapped to warning in the findings ledger
The ledger line uses the scan-provided finding id, unsafe-query, src/db.rs:27, warning, and a concise left: reason
The static rule message and remediation are used when explaining the finding
A repeated finding with the same ID updates the existing line instead of creating a duplicate
Fixed and not-real findings are not persisted
